Franco-Provençal

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Late Latin rīdĕre.

Verb

[edit]

rire (ORB, broad)

  1. to laugh

References

[edit]

  • rire in Lo trèsor Arpitan – on arpitan.eu

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French rire, from Old French rire, from Late Latin rīdere, from Latin rīdēre. The past participle's root-final S was lost.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ʁiʁ/
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (Canada):(file)
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France):(file)
  • Audio (France (Grenoble)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Hérault)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Massy)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iʁ
  • Homophone: rires

Verb

[edit]

rire

  1. to laugh [with de ‘something’]

  1. laugh

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ridre (archaic)

Etymology

[edit]

From Late Latin rīdere, from Latin rīdēre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (archaic) IPA(key): /ˈriðɾə/
  • (classical) IPA(key): /ˈriɾə/

Verb

[edit]

rire

  1. to laugh
    • c. 1200, author unknown, Aucassin et Nicolette:
      [Il] s'en prist a rire
      He started to laugh

Conjugation

[edit]

This verb conjugates as a third-group verb. This verb has irregularities in its conjugation. Old French conjugation varies significantly by date and by region. The following conjugation should be treated as a guide.
